seed_coverage_note: every number in this file covers the seeds listed in seeds_analysed and no others
fields_read_DIRECTLY: release_infeasible_events[*].uncached (the predicted u the re-check used)
share_events[*].qtype / kind / uncached / admitted / reason / w_by_type / key
request.jsonl prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, t_submit, t_first_token, t_done
fields_DERIVED_by_arithmetic_from_direct: prefix_used = est_tokens - uncached (exact on the WARM branch, which is all 34)

PROXIES.proxy: cumulative release_piece piece_tokens whose request row's t_done precedes t_skip
PROXIES.actually_measures: built_tokens is incremented at coordinator.py:1813 inside _settle, so completion time is the right clock; reset at session_end and history_preload.
PROXIES.valid_for_the_claim: YES, and it is VALIDATED here rather than asserted: together with the telemetry reconstruction it must reproduce the DIRECT prefix_used exactly on every row (PC2). It does, 34 of 34 at s4.

PROXIES.proxy: cached_tokens of the last COMPLETED request carrying this session_id before t_skip, with cached_tokens not None
PROXIES.actually_measures: exactly the write site: engine_actions.py:358 sets `session.last_telemetry_cached_tokens = ct` on every completed request that carries a session_id and a usage block, reached from coordinator.py:1702. The guard there is `if sub.session_id:`, which is SESSION-based and not KIND-based, and the belief-apply-off restore at coordinator.py:1708 restores only `belief` and `last_touch_s`, so the field is never clobbered.
PROXIES.valid_for_the_claim: YES, validated by PC2 as above. The request log carries no `kind`, so the kind of each telemetry write is itself joined through decision_id to the decision log's `kind`.

PROXIES.proxy: prompt_tokens and cached_tokens on uo's request row for the SAME opportunity id
PROXIES.actually_measures: the engine's own report of the prefix it held and what it prefilled.
PROXIES.valid_for_the_claim: PARTIALLY, AND THIS IS THE CENTRAL CAVEAT OF THIS DIAGNOSIS. It is the engine's measurement, not a prediction, but it is NOT counterfactually attainable by r1. A recall is the only request that presents the WHOLE history to the engine (a touch sends s.frames[:len(confirmed_bytes_for)], coordinator.py:1120, and a build piece sends only the built prefix), so uo's engine prefix on a session is largely PLANTED BY UO'S OWN EARLIER RECALLS on that session - the very recalls r1 skipped. `prior_uo_recalls_on_session` and `prior_r1_recalls_on_session` are reported on every row so a reader can stratify, and the uncontaminated stratum (prior_uo_recalls == 0) is reported separately.

PROXIES.proxy: max cached_tokens over r1's OWN requests on the same session submitted in [t_skip, t_skip + W]
PROXIES.actually_measures: a LOWER BOUND on the engine's resident prefix for that session in the r1 arm, because cached_tokens <= resident prefix always.
PROXIES.valid_for_the_claim: YES as a lower bound, and only as one. It exists for a minority of rows (the count is reported, never padded), because r1 skipped the later recalls too. Never averaged with the uo proxy.

PROXIES.proxy: the committed scorer's own rule re-derived from uo's outcomes rows
PROXIES.actually_measures: t_delivered - t_opportunity <= deadline_s, after the committed D144 and D146 delivery rewrites (scorer/score.py:539-579).
PROXIES.valid_for_the_claim: YES; the reader's robot_pool_on_time reproduces the committed 118 / 95 / 60 / 35 exactly (PC1), which is what makes the per-skip cost attribution the scorer's and not a near-miss of it.

comparison_validity.decoding: unchanged across the arms: the recall body and its generation settings are coordinator.py's B.RECALL_GEN, which no arm overrides; the arms differ only in release policy and pricing
comparison_validity.caching: PREFIX CACHING IS ENABLED and is load-bearing for this diagnosis, not an incidental detail. Every `cached_tokens` read here is the engine's own report on a LIVE request; nothing is a cold-prefill number and nothing cold is compared with anything warm without saying so. comparison_validity.r1_vs_uo_arm_difference: r1 carries the D179 release re-check and share admission and the D187 (1) cold-pricing fix; uo carries neither gate. So uo is NOT an ablation of r1 by one switch, and the cross-arm engine proxy inherits that: see PROXIES.

fix_candidates.SEED_COVERAGE: every number in this block is seed 4 only, the first seed analysed. The other seeds analysed are reported in seeds[*] and are NOT pooled into these counts.

a_add_tokens_uploaded_since_the_last_com.does_the_bookkeeping_exist: PARTLY. `s.est_tokens` (the current history) and `s.sent_bytes_for` (cstate.py:112) exist, but the prompt of the last completed request is NOT kept on the session: engine_actions.py:358 stores only `cached_tokens`. So this fix needs a NEW field, `last_telemetry_prompt_tokens`, written at the same site.
a_add_tokens_uploaded_since_the_last_com.what_it_would_get_wrong_and_in_which_dir: OVERESTIMATE of the prefix, which is the UNSAFE direction. It asserts that every token uploaded since the last completion is resident, and the measurement here says that is false: on robo001|s000 the code subtracted 5,120 while the session's history was 25,501 tokens, and uo's OWN first recall on that session at the same instant reports the engine holding 6,928, not 25,501. uo's measured first-token time on that opportunity was 4.413 s against 2.953 s of slack, so this candidate converts a skip into a 1.5 s LATE answer on exactly the row it is aimed at.
a_add_tokens_uploaded_since_the_last_com.verdict: DISQUALIFIED by the direction rule, on measured evidence, not on argument

b_use_the_coordinators_own_record_of_wha.what_it_would_get_wrong_and_in_which_dir: OVERESTIMATE, same direction and worse. `sent` is not `resident`: the frozen grid turns its 62,944-token GPU pool over about 89 times in 1,200 s (study_frozen_test.md 17.3, quoted in engine_actions.py), so a frame sent long ago is routinely evicted. It would also double-count frames re-sent as bytes after a 400 (racefix_bytes_resent).

c_running_max.what: take the running maximum of last_telemetry_cached_tokens instead of the last
c_running_max.what_it_would_get_wrong_and_in_which_dir: OVERESTIMATE after an eviction, since a maximum never falls. But it does not arise: the measured gain is zero, because `prefix_used = max(built_tokens, last telemetry)` already dominates every earlier telemetry value on all of these rows.
c_running_max.verdict: REJECTED: measured gain is zero, so it is not a fix at all

THE_FINDING_THAT_DISPLACES_ALL_THREE.what_the_measurement_says: the prefix the code subtracts is NOT materially wrong in the r1 arm. Only 9 of 34 skips were refused by the size term at all; the other 25 were refused by the QUEUE term b2*queued_uncached_ahead, where the predicted u is already small. And of the size-decided skips, almost all sit on sessions on which r1 had never released a recall, so the engine genuinely did not hold the history: the 6.4x ratio against uo is largely uo's own earlier recalls on those sessions, not a pricing residue.
THE_FINDING_THAT_DISPLACES_ALL_THREE.the_mechanism_named: a recall is the ONLY request that presents the whole history to the engine. A touch sends s.frames[:len(confirmed_bytes_for)] (coordinator.py:1118-1127) and a build piece sends the built prefix plus one slice (coordinator.py:1197-1204), so neither can ever report, or create, a prefix larger than the built prefix. The re-check at coordinator.py:1277-1296 prices a recall on its OWN first-token feasibility and is blind to the prefix that sending it PLANTS for that session's later recalls. Skipping the first recall on a session therefore keeps the session cold, which keeps the next recall expensive, which skips it again.

the_smallest_honest_fix.statement: exempt a session's FIRST whole-history recall from the release re-check, once per session, and let the re-check govern every later recall unchanged.
the_smallest_honest_fix.file_line: experiments/orchestration/live2/coordinator.py:1277, the `if self._release_recheck:` guard in `_submit_recall`; the condition becomes `if self._release_recheck and not s.whole_history_sent:` with the flag set beside `self._uncached_in_flight += int(_uncached)` at coordinator.py:1319 and cleared where `built_tokens` is reset (coordinator.py:757).
the_smallest_honest_fix.why_it_is_the_smallest: it changes NO price, NO coefficient, NO floor, NO W_max and NO deadline; it changes the number of times the re-check is consulted on a session from every recall to every recall after the first. It is a RELEASE-POLICY change and therefore a NEW LABELLED VERSION under D187, not an implementation fix.
the_smallest_honest_fix.what_it_gets_wrong_and_in_which_directio: it admits a request the predictor says is infeasible, so it spends LATENESS and it spends CAPACITY. The lateness side is measured and is cheaper than it looks: all 34 skips are outcomes rows with t_delivered None and 0 of them are scored on time, so a skip is already a guaranteed miss on the robot axis, and turning one into a late cloud answer cannot lower robot_pool_on_time. The REAL price is paid on the other axes through the capacity the admitted recall consumes: uo, which has no re-check at all, has dashcam_all_meet FALSE where r1 has TRUE. That is the trade this fix makes, stated as a trade and not as a free gain.

what_it_does_NOT_address_stated_before_t.why: on those sessions the prefix the code subtracted is close to what r1's own engine probe reports and the size term already fits the slack; the refusal is b2 * queued_uncached_ahead. A bootstrap exemption does nothing for them.
what_it_does_NOT_address_stated_before_t.honest_arithmetic_on_the_bar: the exemption can recover at most the skips on never-warmed sessions LESS one per such session (the exempted recall itself is predicted infeasible and uo's measured first-token times on those first recalls, 4.4 to 5.5 s, say it would arrive late): at s4 that is 15 minus 5 sessions. So this fix ALONE does NOT reach the bar of at most 13, and is not offered as if it did. It is the smallest change that attacks the mechanism the measurement actually identifies.
what_it_does_NOT_address_stated_before_t.register: a constructed bound from measured counts, not a predicted result

the_smallest_honest_fix.the_bound_that_must_be_stated_with_it: at most one extra admission per robot session, so at most 9 extra recalls at s4 against the 34 skips. This is a CONSTRUCTED BOUND from the session count, not a measured count of what would happen.

pre_registered_pass_check.primary: release_infeasible_recall at s4 falls from 34 to at most 13, the unchanged pre-registered bar from c7c60e5b
pre_registered_pass_check.secondary: robot_pool_on_time at s4 rises from 95 toward 118 and retains at least 90 percent of uo's gain over base, i.e. at least 0.90 * (118 - 35) + 35 = 110 of 132
pre_registered_pass_check.FAILURE_CONDITION_that_must_be_reported_: if release_infeasible_recall falls but robot_pool_on_time does not rise to match, the admitted recalls are arriving late and the named explanation is wrong
pre_registered_pass_check.the_control_that_must_hold: dashcam_all_meet stays TRUE and ss_pool_on_time does not fall below 355 of 357 at s4. If either moves, the fix bought the robot axis with the axes the share gate exists to protect, and must be reported as a trade-off ablation and not as a fix.
pre_registered_pass_check.the_positive_control_on_the_check_itself: re-score covex-v6-state-uo and hybrid-F-lhreq-noc3 at s4 with the same reader and require 118 and 35 exactly before the new cell is read

the_upper_bound_a_perfect_prefix_would_b.register: a CONSTRUCTED BOUND under a counterfactual the arm cannot realise, because the engine prefix it uses is uo's and was planted by uo's own earlier recalls. It is the ceiling on any prefix-estimation fix, not a target.
